title: Google AI Courses 2026: Free Learning, Badges & Where to Start
summary: Seven Google Skills courses to explore, the difference between badges and certificates, and practical advice for African students.
description: A verification-first guide to seven Google AI learning opportunities and their credentials.
author: ApplyMate Editorial

source.sourceAttribution: Opportunity discovered via Fully Scholarships; application links point to Google Skills.

claims.text: The listed micro-courses offer skill badges rather than all representing free professional certificates.
No fixed application deadline was identified for the self-paced courses.

eligibility.requirements: Google Skills account; individual course requirements vary.
eligibility.uncertainty: Individual labs and advanced credentials may require credits or subscription.

sections.heading: What is actually free?
paragraphs: Google Skills lists short AI learning modules covering generative AI, large language models, image generation, attention, encoder-decoder architectures and Vertex AI. The original roundup describes these as free learning opportunities. Check each course page before assuming every hands-on lab or certificate on the wider platform is free.
A Google Skills badge is different from a certificate or professional certification. Be precise when listing credentials on your CV.

sections.heading: Where to start
paragraphs: Beginners can start with Introduction to Generative AI, then move to Large Language Models. If you want to understand the models, explore Attention and Encoder-Decoder Architecture. If your goal is building practical applications, move toward Vertex AI Studio.

courses.name: Introduction to Generative AI
courses.description: Generative AI concepts and how the field differs from traditional machine learning.

courses.name: Introduction to Large Language Models
courses.description: LLM basics, uses, prompt tuning and Google development tools.

courses.name: Introduction to Image Generation
courses.description: Diffusion models and the principles behind modern image generation.

courses.name: Encoder-Decoder Architecture
courses.description: Sequence-to-sequence tasks and a TensorFlow walkthrough.

courses.name: Attention Mechanism
courses.description: How models focus on important parts of an input sequence.

courses.name: Create Image Captioning Models
courses.description: Image-captioning model architecture, training and evaluation.

courses.name: Introduction to Vertex AI Studio
courses.description: Multimodal Gemini prototyping, prompt design and model tuning.

sections.heading: The Scholarz 1 + 1 rule
paragraphs: One badge plus one proof of work. After an LLM course, document a prompt experiment. After image generation, compare results. After Vertex AI Studio, prototype something useful.
For Zimbabwean and other African learners, short online modules offer a low-cost way to explore AI, but a finished project often says more than a list of unattended courses.

sections.heading: Deadline and limitations
paragraphs: No fixed deadline was identified for the listed self-paced courses. Access, badges, credits and fees can change, so check the official Google Skills page before enrolling.
